newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana's brother wins libel damages in UK.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana's brother wins libel damages in UK.

text.p: The aristocratic brother of Princess Diana accepted an apology and undisclosed libel damages in England's High Court on Wednesday over newspaper allegations about his attempts to curb the activities of a South African photographer.
Earl Spencer lives in South Africa, as do his estranged wife Victoria and their four children. He was suing Britain's Guardian and Evening Standard newspapers over stories published in 1996.
Lawyers for the earl, Diana's younger brother, told the court the family had been subjected to a "persistent and relentless campaign of intimidation" by freelance photographer Fanie Jason.

They said Jason had gained unlawful access to Spencer's home, taken photographs of his wife while she was swimming in the pool, and insinuated that he would make use of the photographs unless she cooperated with him.

When the earl took out injunctions against the photographer in a South African court, articles in the Guardian and the Evening Standard implied that he was seeking a curtailment of South Africa's press freedom laws for his own purposes.
Lawyer Simon Ekins told the court the article in the Guardian "portrayed Jason as a heoric figure, stressed his impoverished origins and the fact that he was black".
Lawyers for the two newspapers accepted that there was no truth in the defamatory imputations published, and sincerely apologised for the embarrassment and distress caused.
They agreed to pay Spencer substantial damages and his legal costs. The earl was not in court for the hearing.
